name:
  Cortex
timeline:
  Mar 2026 - Present
context:
  Started as a self-initiated project to build a production-grade internal AI knowledge system that enables organizations to securely store, retrieve, and reason over organizational knowledge using Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG).
objective:
  To build an AI-powered enterprise knowledge platform that delivers accurate, source-grounded answers through hybrid retrieval, reranking, and role-based access control.
current_status:
  Actively under development with a functional end-to-end RAG pipeline and ongoing feature enhancements.
implemented_features:
  Document ingestion with metadata extraction and versioning
  Hybrid retrieval using semantic search, PostgreSQL full-text search, and Reciprocal Rank Fusion (RRF)
  Cross-encoder reranking for improved retrieval quality
  Role-based document access and project-level permissions
  Source-cited AI responses with conversation history
  Document management and knowledge base administration
  Comprehensive retrieval evaluation framework with automated metrics
technical_approach:
  Built a production-oriented RAG pipeline where documents are chunked, embedded, stored using pgvector, retrieved through hybrid search, reranked, and passed to an LLM for grounded response generation while enforcing access control.
tech_stack:
  frontend:
    React
  backend:
    FastAPI (Python)
  database:
    PostgreSQL + pgvector
  storage:
    Supabase Storage
  authentication:
    JWT
  ai_stack:
    Gemini Embeddings, LLM APIs, Hybrid RAG, Cross-Encoder Reranker
  deployment:
    Docker, Render, Vercel
key_challenges:
  Designing an effective hybrid retrieval pipeline
  Balancing retrieval quality with inference latency
  Implementing scalable document versioning and access control
learning_outcomes:
  Deep understanding of production RAG system design
  Experience evaluating retrieval using Recall@K, MRR, and nDCG
  Learned the trade-offs between retrieval quality, reranking, and response latency
recognition:
  Evaluation showed that integrating a cross-encoder reranker improved Recall@7 from 0.8995 to 0.9459, MRR from 0.7560 to 0.9019, and nDCG@7 from 0.7578 to 0.8839, demonstrating substantially better retrieval quality with an increase in average latency (5.67s → 9.03s).
links:
  https://github.com/Pratham9911/Cortex/

context:
  Designing Cortex from scratch
difficulty:
  There was no single correct architecture for building the retrieval system. I had to decide how documents should be processed, stored, searched, and ranked with very limited prior experience.
how_it_affected_me:
  I spent significant time researching different approaches before writing production code.
how_i_handled_it:
  I broke the problem into smaller parts, studied engineering blogs, videos, and real-world architectures, compared trade-offs, and built prototypes before making final decisions.
what_i_learned:
  When working with uncertainty, structured research and experimentation lead to better technical decisions than rushing into implementation.

context:
  Working on a real software product during my internship
difficulty:
  The initial requirements were not fully defined, and different team members had different ideas about how the system should work.
how_it_affected_me:
  Development could have become inconsistent because everyone had a different understanding of the product.
how_i_handled_it:
  We divided ownership by modules, researched our respective domains, discussed ideas with mentors and stakeholders, and refined requirements through regular feedback sessions.
what_i_learned:
  Building real software is an iterative process that depends on communication, feedback, and collaboration as much as technical skills.

context:
  Leading a team during the AI for Climate Change Hackathon
difficulty:
  Although I divided the work among team members, I didn't track progress regularly while everyone was busy with assignments and exams.
how_it_affected_me:
  We discovered delays too late and had to simplify the final solution before submission.
how_i_handled_it:
  I took responsibility, completed the most important parts, and later changed the way I managed teams by introducing regular milestones and progress reviews.
what_i_learned:
  Leadership is not only about assigning work but also about continuously checking progress and supporting the team throughout the project.
